knowledge_checks.title: Active Recall: 3.1.6
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. Which statement correctly describes the bootstrap move for estimating properties of an estimator?
hints: Use the concept from this learning objective only.
knowledge_checks.explanation: Bootstrap for estimator properties resamples, recomputes the estimator many times, and summarises the replicates. Asymptotic Normal laws and bootstrap confidence intervals are related but distinct ideas; one replicate is not a property estimate.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: Resample, recompute the estimator, summarise replicates (e.g. SE or bias).
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Equating bootstrap property estimation with asymptotics or with bootstrap CI construction.

choices.label: Resample from the observed sample (with replacement, under the usual nonparametric bootstrap), recompute the estimator on each resample, and summarise the replicate distribution (for example to estimate standard error or bias).
Replace the estimator by its asymptotic Normal approximation; that replacement is what 'bootstrap' means for estimator properties.
Form a confidence interval from bootstrap percentiles; estimating an estimator's standard error is the same learning objective as building that interval.
Bootstrap means drawing a single new sample from the fitted parametric model and reporting that one replicate as the property estimate.

knowledge_checks.title: Checkpoint: 3.1.6
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. You have an estimator θ̂ from a sample of size n. Which statement correctly describes using the bootstrap to estimate the standard error of θ̂?
knowledge_checks.body: Bootstrap SE procedure; refuse asymptotics-as-bootstrap and CI-as-same.
hints: Use the concept from this learning objective only.
knowledge_checks.explanation: Bootstrap SE uses the spread of many with-replacement replicates of θ̂. Asymptotic variance plug-ins and bootstrap CI construction are different procedures.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: With-replacement resamples → θ̂* replicates → empirical SD as SE; distinct from asymptotics and from bootstrap CIs.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Calling an asymptotic plug-in or a CI half-width 'the bootstrap SE'.

choices.label: Draw many resamples with replacement from the original sample, recompute θ̂* on each resample, and use the empirical standard deviation of the θ̂* values as the SE estimate. That is not the same as quoting an asymptotic Normal law, and not the same as constructing a bootstrap confidence interval.
Compute the asymptotic variance 1/(n I(θ̂)) once; that single plug-in is the bootstrap standard error by definition.
Form the percentile bootstrap confidence interval and report half its width as the only legitimate bootstrap standard error.
Resample without replacement until the resample has size n/2, compute one θ̂*, and take |θ̂* − θ̂| as the standard error.

worked_example.title: Bootstrap SE of mean claim severity
worked_example.problem_statement: A nonparametric bootstrap of the sample mean claim severity produced B = 5 bootstrap replicates (£00): 210, 195, 220, 205, 200. Estimate the bootstrap standard error of the mean using SÊ_boot = √[(1/B) Σ(θ̂*_b − θ̄*)²], where θ̄* is the mean of the bootstrap replicates.
worked_example.attempt_before_reveal: CMP closed. First compute θ̄*, then the average squared deviation.

steps.label: Mean of bootstrap replicates
steps.explanation: θ̄* centres the bootstrap deviations used in the SE formula.

steps.label: Sum of squared deviations
steps.explanation: Each replicate's squared distance from θ̄* enters the bootstrap variance.

steps.label: Bootstrap SE
steps.explanation: The stated bootstrap SE divides by B inside the square root.

worked_example.common_pitfall: Dividing by B−1 = 4 (ordinary sample SD) to get √(370/4) = √92.5 ≈ 9.62 instead of the bootstrap /B form √(370/5) = √74 required here.
